section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the relationships between psychological flexibility, self-compassion (engagement and action), and body appreciation in adult women. The study used path analysis to test whether psychological inflexibility mediates the association between self-compassionate engagement and action, with results indicating that self-compassionate action and psychological inflexibility are direct predictors of body appreciation. The authors acknowledge several limitations including the cross-sectional correlational design, the female-only sample, and the use of self-report measures and snowball sampling, while suggesting that future research should explore these mechanisms in mixed-gender and adolescent populations.

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the role of affect regulation mechanisms (psychological flexibility, self-compassionate engagement, and self-compassionate action) in predicting body appreciation (measured via BAS-2) in adult women. The path model (Fig. 1) reveals that self-compassionate action and psychological inflexibility directly predict body appreciation, while self-compassionate engagement operates indirectly through these mechanisms, with a direct negative association between BMI and body appreciation (r = -0.28***).
